data.title: Uniswap Adds 2,295 New Wallets in Four-Year High as UNI Slides Below $7. Analyst Forecasts $10 to $12 UNI Price.
data.description:
Uniswap (UNI-USD) added 2,295 new wallets in a single day, reaching its fastest network growth since November 2022 even as the token dropped 25.75% over the past month to $6.93.

UNI fell 1.2% over the past 24 hours. On-chain analytics firm Santiment reports that the jump in first-time UNI addresses could build a price floor if new wallet creation stays high.

Uniswap v4 Drives New Wallet Growth

Santiment linked the four-year high in new users to new Uniswap v4 features, broader liquidity routing, and ongoing work on the Unichain layer-2 network. DefiLlama data shows Uniswap v4 now holds about $1.44 billion in total value locked, marking a 17% increase over the past month.

"Holding $7 while network growth remains above its recent baseline would favor another test of $8, while losing $7 alongside fading wallet creation would suggest the spike was mostly short-term excitement rather than sustained adoption," Santiment wrote in a post.

Unichain and Token Burns Cut Network Costs

Datawallet reports that Uniswap v4 runs on more than 15 networks, including Ethereum, Base, Arbitrum, and Unichain. The v4 upgrade uses a single contract design that cuts liquidity pool creation costs by 99% and lowers gas fees on multi-hop token swaps.

Following a December 2025 governance vote, the protocol also collects fees from v2 and selected v3 pools to burn UNI tokens across expanding chains.

Meanwhile, Uniswap Labs built its DeFi-focused Unichain layer-2 network on the OP Stack with one-second block times and gas costs about 95% lower than Ethereum. Across Protocol data shows Uniswap v4 on Unichain holds around $369 million in total value locked after launching its mainnet in February 2025.

Analysts Are Looking at the $7 UNI Price Level

Market analysts remain split on UNI's next price move after the token slipped below the $7 mark. Analyst Phoenix noted that seller pressure grew after UNI tested $10, pushing the price below the Ichimoku cloud and its moving averages on falling trading volume. Phoenix warned that a full drop below $7 could send UNI down toward $6 to $6.50.

Santiment identified $7.50 as the first key level for UNI to win back, followed by $8. Other market watchers still see room for a rebound if the wider crypto market steadies. On October 21, when UNI traded above $7, analyst Scient pointed to bullish four-hour chart patterns and suggested a possible price squeeze similar to Zcash (ZEC-USD).

Analyst Defi Rocketeer expects a retest of $10 to $12 if market conditions calm down, while analyst CryptoBullet placed major upward resistance between $13 and $15.

At the time of writing, UNI token's price is trading near $6.87.
data.author: Annika Masrani

data.title: Meta's AI Financing Plan Gives Muse More Upside and Shareholders More Risk
data.description:
Social media giant Meta Platforms (META) is creating nonvoting shares that can help finance its AI expansion without reducing Mark Zuckerberg's voting control. An October 21 filing said that three internal forecast cases called for hundreds of billions of dollars in financing over several years, with the need starting as early as fall 2026. As a result, Muse will need to become a large profit source if shareholders are going to earn a strong return on Meta's spending, especially since it comes with dilution risks.

The Class C shares are scheduled to come into effect on January 19, 2027. Meta would then distribute one Class C share for every Class A or Class B share. The first distribution works like a two-for-one split and raises no money. Nevertheless, Meta could later issue additional Class C shares to raise capital.

Catalysts that May Push the Stock Higher

Muse provides Meta with a solid path to earn a return on that new capital. More than 10 million people in the U.S. and Canada set up the AI assistant within roughly six weeks. About 25% use it on a typical day. Shopping is the most common use, with more than one-quarter of weekly users shopping through Muse and an average purchase above $200.

Promotion

High conviction META bears now have this Tradr ETF

Those purchases are customer spending rather than Meta revenue. Still, they create a way to monetize the app in the future because Meta plans to collect fees from businesses when Muse helps complete a transaction. Paid subscriptions provide a second path, while business services could eventually add recurring revenue.

Meta also has evidence that AI can improve its advertising business. The company estimates that advertisers that followed recommendations from its AI business assistant generated almost 5% more conversions at the same cost and increased their ad spending by 9% versus similar nonusers. That matters because advertising produced $63.1 billion of Q3 revenue. Therefore, even small improvements can have a large financial effect at that scale.

Risks to Watch Out For

Nevertheless, Meta is spending the money way before Muse has proven it is profitable. More specifically, the firm expects $135 billion to $145 billion in 2026 capital spending, which is up $5 billion at the lower end of its prior range. During Q3, cash flow from operations of $32.79 billion did not cover $34.91 billion in capital spending and finance lease principal payments. Free cash flow was therefore -$2.12 billion.

Additionally, future Class C sales could dilute each investor's share of Meta's profits while protecting Zuckerberg's control, thanks to the nonvoting structure. For context, Zuckerberg held 60.6% of Meta's voting power as of October 1.

Muse is also very expensive to operate, as its computing demands have delayed a global launch. Meta expects to improve its cost efficiency by more than tenfold over the next year, and if those savings arrive, the app would become more profitable as subscriptions and transaction fees grow. However, if they don't, each wave of new users could increase Meta's cash needs before Muse can add meaningful bottom-line growth.

What Is the Price Target for Meta?

Overall, analysts have a Strong Buy consensus rating on META stock based on 38 Buys, six Holds, and zero Sells assigned in the past three months, as indicated by the graphic below. Furthermore, the average META price target of $851.03 per share implies 32.5% upside potential. (See META Stock Forecast).

data.title: M&A News: Instacart Stock (CART) Jumps 10% on Takeover Rumors
data.description:
Instacart's (CART) stock closed 10% higher on Oct. 23 as rumors of a takeover swirl around the company. Multiple media reports say that the grocery-delivery company is exploring a sale and has had held preliminary discussions with rivals Uber (UBER) and DoorDash (DASH) about a potential takeover.

Instacart, also known as Maplebear, is currently valued at about $12 billion and is reportedly working with an investment bank to evaluate its options, according to media reports. A typical takeover premium of 30% to 40% would put its valuation at as much as $17 billion, though discussions reportedly are in the preliminary stages and no deal has been announced.

data.title: Bitcoin (BTC) Grinds Lower As Market Selloff Worsens
data.description:
Bitcoin (BTC) slid lower on Oct. 23 as the selloff in stocks worsened and spread to most sectors of the market. BTC was down 0.30% at $81,250 at the end of the trading session for equity markets. The largest cryptocurrency by market capitalization is down 5% in October as volatility intensifies and investors head for the safety of government Treasury bonds.

The drop in Bitcoin on Oct. 23 comes on a day when the blue-chip Dow Jones Industrial Average closed 652 points lower and a day after the technology-laden Nasdaq Composite dropped nearly 700 points on Oct. 22. A growing number of issues are impacting risk assets such as technology stocks and cryptocurrencies, including worries about the artificial intelligence (AI) trade, oil prices, and bond yields.

The U.S. is deploying additional troops and military equipment to the Middle East as Iran threatens to target energy infrastructure, airports, and U.S. military bases across the region if Washington and Israel resume attacks, according to the Wall Street Journal.
  • U.S. Ambassador to the UN Mike Waltz said the U.S.-Iran war could last another year if Iran refuses to come to the negotiating table. "I'm not going to put out hypotheticals," he told the Financial Times. "One would hope that they'll come to the table in a meaningful way before that."
  • Long-dated Treasury yields resumed their uptrend following a selloff on Thursday. The 10-year yield rose 4.4 basis points (bps) to 4.99%, while the 30-year yield climbed 3.8 bps to 5.32%.
  • The University of Michigan's Index of Consumer Sentiment for October came in at 48.0, topping the estimate of 46.3 but slipping slightly from 48.1 in September. The reading remains at a five-month low as concerns over affordability and the economic outlook persist. Furthermore, year-ahead inflation expectations climbed to 4.7% from 4.6% in September, while long-term expectations increased to 3.5% from 3.4%.
  • Apple (AAPL) briefly overtook Nvidia (NVDA) in intraday trading to become the world's most valuable publicly traded company by market capitalization. That came after NVDA stock received a rare "Sell" rating from Seaport Research.
  • American Express (AXP) CEO Steve Squeri said that the company will cut approximately 5% of its global workforce to "take advantage of AI in the coming quarters and the coming years."
  • Several companies will report their earnings next week, including Microsoft (MSFT), Visa (V), Alphabet (GOOGL), and Starbucks (SBUX). Furthermore, the Fed will announce its interest rate decision on Wednesday, October 28.

data.title: IREN Stock: Why Analysts Still See Over 200% Upside Despite This Week's Plunge
data.description:
IREN Limited shares (IREN) sold off this week, down more than 21% in the past five days alone. This came amid fresh concerns about high borrowing costs in the neocloud and larger tech industry. Still, the analyst consensus rating on IREN stock suggests about 228% upside. Analysts have pointed to the company's customer deals, stronger GPU leasing pricing, and power portfolio.

What Are IREN Bulls Saying?

Notably, four-star JPMorgan analyst Richard Choe recently upgraded IREN stock from Sell to Buy. Choe lifted his price target from $46 to $65, suggesting 155% upside.

The analyst noted that IREN's recent deals and AI push have helped it become "a formidable neocloud" company. He also noted that the company now gets "substantially" better deals for its GPU and power capacity. For instance, Choe noted that IREN's AI cloud contracts have gone from $10-$15/W to $15-20/W or higher.

Promotion

Similarly,  BTIG's five-star analyst Gregory Lewis recently reaffirmed his Buy rating on IREN. He also set a price target of $80, suggesting about 214% upside. Lewis noted that IREN stands out with its 5 gigawatts of potential power capacity.

The analyst believes that IREN's control of its supply chain makes its potential power capacity unique compared to its peers. IREN secures land, builds data centers, secures power, and even purchases GPU capacity and other hardware for its facilities.

Why Some Analysts Remain Cautious

Meanwhile, a few analysts have decided to tread cautiously on IREN shares. For instance, Jones Trading analyst Kevin Dede rated IREN stock a Hold. The analyst noted that he finds a few factors about IREN "polarizing." For example, the analyst argued that IREN has a broad customer base but lower-quality customers.

Similarly, Rothschild & Co. Redburn analyst Alexander Haissl also issued a Hold rating on IREN shares. At the current price, Haissl believes investors have sufficiently priced in IREN's risk and likely returns.

Is IREN a Good Stock to Buy Now?

On Wall Street, analysts now rate IREN's shares a Strong Buy. This consensus reflects eight Buys and two Holds assigned over the past three months.

In addition, the average IREN price target of $82.56 implies about 228% upside ahead (see IREN stock forecast here).
